doors.label: Tax cap
doors.sentence: Voted NO on the 7.28% aggregate / 9.34% residential 2026 budget because it was too low: "It's so funny to me that we're at each other's throats about this when the system itself is just flawed. We're being asked to tax in a way that just sucks." Also voted NO on the Nov 2025 reduction that would have held the increase to 4%.

doors.label: Downtown order
doors.sentence: Lone NO on the daytime-sheltering enforcement motion, 8–1. Voted YES on formalising the overnight-sheltering ban in Topaz, Hollywood and Regatta Point parks. No Public Order Team or bylaw-hours position in any 2026 text.

doors.label: Housing
doors.sentence: Named YES on Missing Middle (6–3), on the Delegation Bylaw aligning land use with provincial housing statutes (8–1), on the Official Community Plan (5–3), and on reducing minimum parking requirements (6–3). No Kim-owned 2026 housing sentence.

cells.quote: Four named supply votes. Missing Middle 6–3: the policy "up-zones single-family residential lots to allow townhouses, triplexes, and houseplexes to be built without going through the council rezoning or public hearing process." Plus Delegation Bylaw 8–1, OCP 5–3, parking-minimum reduction 6–3.
cells.why: Commits + comparable instrument: real supply, not M6's composition shares or quarterly target reporting. No sourced miss on this cell.

cells.quote: YES on the Delegation Bylaw, 8–1: council "adopts the Delegation Bylaw and updated associated land-use bylaws" to "better align its land-use regulations with provincial housing statutes that were enacted to speed up the pace of homebuilding.
cells.why: Commits + comparable: a genuine approval-speed instrument. No published category benchmarks, which is the other half of M7.

cells.quote: YES 8–1 on the DCC waiver: "Council approves a new grant policy that offsets the City's Development Cost Charges (DCCs) for eligible below-market housing projects." M8's named instrument is "targeted DCC reductions." Comparable rather than same: hers is below-market rather than purpose-built rental, and carries no published infrastructure funding plan.
On the Feb 2025 police-staffing vote she advocated redirecting funds "toward alternative services like housing, social support programs, harm reduction efforts, and mental health resources.
cells.why: Agrees on the goal, names no instrument: no crisis-response capacity, no published dispatch criteria, no diversion figure. The slate's "24-hour mental health crisis response" is we, held under Ruling 1.

cells.quote: Coun. Susan Kim, the lone vote against the motion
cells.why: on stepped-up daytime sheltering enforcement, 8–1: "It's just not enough because I don't believe that the deus ex machina we're waiting for is going to come." The tracker records her argument that accelerating enforcement was a band-aid that would "simply disperse vulnerable people and disconnect them from critical social and health services." A recorded vote against the cell's own instrument.

cells.what: drug-use buffer (City: list + bylaw/DPOT + VicPD/CDSA; not City seizure)

cells.quote: YES 8–1 on "formally implementing the official bylaw change … of banning overnight sheltering at Topaz Park, Hollywood Park, and Regatta Point Park," and YES 7–2 on permanently prohibiting overnight sheltering in those parks "conditional on finding alternative housing options for the occupants.
cells.why: Commits + comparable: park-specific prohibitions rather than M34's rapid-removal protocol. Her daytime-enforcement NO is scored on row 10 and shown here as context only.

cells.what: tax glide path (capped on the residential rate)
cells.quote: It's so funny to me that we're at each other's throats about this when the system itself is just flawed. We're being asked to tax in a way that just sucks.
cells.why: Voted NO on the 2026 budget (7.28% aggregate, 9.34% residential) on the ground that the increase was too low, and NO in Nov 2025 on reducing infrastructure funding "from $5.5 million to $4 million to help cap the city's property tax increase at 4%." Two recorded votes against a residential-rate cap.

cells.quote: YES 7–2: council "voted to urge BC Housing and Island Health to provide supportive housing and treatment for individuals sleeping downtown, citing an emergency." Also YES 7–2 on requesting stable provincial active-transportation funding, 15 Jun 2026.
cells.why: Commits, but neither instrument: no quarterly downloading ledger, no twice-yearly UBCM/FCM resolutions, no published refusal threshold.

cells.what: CRD cost and the Goldstream plant
business, downtown, one mandate not a new office
cells.quote: YES 7–2, 25 Jul 2026: council "supported measures to encourage new hotel construction in the central business district, including increased non-residential density and temporary property-tax exemption for qualifying hotels.
cells.why: Commits + comparable: a real tax-base and tourism instrument inside the campaign year, but not M71's storefront-vacancy target or M73b's single mandate.

cells.what: capital threshold, short-stay parking (15-min grace; first-hour gated Year 2), permit fees
Host Nations Foundation. Topic never drops out of the 12. A dash is still allowed on M1–M5.
tenant protections, STR, indoor heat (M9c struck; 26°C gated)
cells.quote: YES 7–2 on the Displaced Tenant Assistance Compensation policy, and part of the unanimous 30 Jul 2026 council decision raising moving-expense compensation for long-term tenants displaced by redevelopment. M9's named instrument is "moving-cost compensation indexed to local rents.
cells.why: Commits + same instrument, inside the campaign year. No sourced miss on this cell.

cells.quote: YES 6–3 on a "permanent 40-unit supportive housing facility at 225 Russell Street"; YES 6–3 on zoning "allowing temporary social-services centres and shelters to operate in any city neighbourhood without undergoing a site-specific public rezoning process"; YES 6–2 on $100,000 stop-gap funding for Our Place Society.
cells.why: Commits + comparable: the Housing First siting half is there, the STEP throughput and published cost-per-placement half is not.

cells.what: childcare, doctors, youth (M13 school food is $0 → M13d)

cells.quote: YES 7–2 on the Pandora cleanup pilot: "A locking dumpster will be placed on the slip road alongside Pandora, and members of the street community will be paid a stipend to do waste collection in the area in a $9,000 pilot project.
cells.why: Commits + comparable: a funded street-cleanliness instrument, but not M14's 48-hour graffiti standard or M17's extended sanitation hours.

cells.what: mobility + Vision Zero (M39 30 km/h struck; calming is M38)
cells.quote: YES 6–3 on the 2023–2027 financial plan's active-transportation allocation, on the argument that "bundling bike network construction with planned underground utility and road repaving projects reduces long-term construction costs.
cells.why: Commits + comparable: funds the protected-network build (M41), but no Vision Zero intersection programme, no safety-audit rule. M39 is struck and not scored.

cells.what: walking and transit the City controls

cells.quote: Her 2022 plank treating public bathrooms as transportation infrastructure is the plank the Program absorbed as M24b.
cells.why: 2022 campaign text counts as Record for an incumbent, shown not scored. No 2022–26 vote and no 2026 sentence on washroom spacing or an accessibility audit.

cells.what: VicPD funding + regional review (convene-and-publish; no binding other force)
cells.quote: Three named votes, none of them on this cell's instrument.
cells.why: NO on the $62.27M 2024 VicPD provisional budget, 6–3, on concern about "over-indexing city revenues into policing at the expense of social services, affordable housing, and harm-reduction initiatives." NO on police staffing, 7–2: "83% of public submissions regarding policing explicitly opposed a police budget increase." YES 5–4 to cut the VicPD request by roughly $344,000, reducing four new officers to two. Shown, not scored: M29 is the Esquimalt cost-share formula and M29b is a convened regional review. She has taken no position on either. Funding level is adjacent, and adjacency is not a source.

cells.what: safety dashboard, published enforcement record, crime target
cells.quote: YES 8–1 adopting the Community Safety and Well-Being Plan.
cells.why: Commits, but neither instrument: M31c's demand is to retrofit that plan into a performance contract with five mandatory fields and quarterly outcome reporting. No dashboard, no published enforcement record, no crime-reduction target anywhere in her record.

cells.quote: YES 7–2 on the downtown cinema retention strategy: "Victoria to look at how to keep, attract movie theatres as Odeon goes on market," prompted by the Cineplex Odeon, "a fixture downtown since 1948," listed at $8.5 million.
cells.why: Commits + comparable: a cultural-venue retention instrument, but not M46b's designated list, right of first refusal, permissive tax exemption or lease-bridge fund.

cells.what: culture, sport, and the arts funding floor
cells.quote: YES 7–2 on a one-time $175,000 grant from contingency for the Victoria Curling Club ice-plant replacement, supporters citing "a vital community hub serving thousands of members.
cells.why: Commits + comparable: a sport-facility capital instrument, but not M52's Royal Athletic Park restoration or M50b's arts funding floor. Recused on the FernFest grant, 9 May 2026.

cells.quote: NO in Nov 2025 on reducing infrastructure funding "from $5.5 million to $4 million to help cap the city's property tax increase at 4%"; the tracker records that she "resists scaling back city investments and services to satisfy low property tax targets." On 7 May 2026 she also said "The benefit of this exercise this year … we actually did find places we could cut back reasonably." Shown, not scored: neither touches a rotating zero-based review of 200+ programmes, and the second line raises the topic without naming a goal or an action.
cells.why: Mentions does not resolve up.

cells.what: local-tech procurement, open data, Wi-Fi, EV charging
trees, mode share, ecosystems, emergency preparedness

cells.quote: YES 7–2 on changes to the Requests to Address Council Policy that "reduced the individual speaking allotment from 5 minutes to 3 minutes per speaker" and capped commentary at six speakers per meeting.
cells.why: Shown, not scored: M79's instrument is a draft-back standard and a timed written response to consultation, not speaking time. No position on an Integrity Commissioner or the MNP recommendations.

cells.quote: Voted against limiting council salary increases to CPI, motion failed 3–6, 15 Nov 2025.
cells.why: Shown, not scored: M79f's instrument is deferral of any remuneration change to the start of the following term, not a CPI cap, and the Program "takes no position on whether Council remuneration is currently too high or too low." Adjacency is not a source. No position on a lobbyist registry or the FOI application fee.

cells.what: neighbourhoods, language access, Local Area Plans
cells.quote: YES 5–3 adopting the Official Community Plan, 2 Oct 2025.
cells.why: Her 2022 plank on non-English grant applications is the plank the Program absorbed as M80b. Shown, not scored: the Program explicitly declines OCP repeal-and-replace and asks instead for a rolling two-plans-per-year Local Area Plan programme, on which she has no position; and 2022 text is Record only. She is Neighbourhood Liaison for Hillside Quadra, but holding a seat is not a source.

cells.what: community surveys, turnout and ballot access
Saanich amalgamation (one line, not the whole topic)
cells.quote: YES 5–4 to place the non-binding question "Do you support Saanich and Victoria becoming one municipality?" on the 17 Oct 2026 ballot.
cells.why: Commits, but neither instrument: no 90-day publication against the Minister's conditions, no joint analysis commissioned with Saanich, no First Nations consultation step, no return to the Province for a binding referendum.
